limitations: Current geometry is unconfirmed. All statistics describe raw ranges, report repeatability, ages and availability; there are no bias or absolute position-error claims.

Only each actual USB observer's own reports support filter comparisons. N1 zero coordinates are imposed. N3 remains baseline firmware on its power bank; forwarded N3 reports do not measure a filtered hardware N3.

A1 has no fresh restart. B and A2 each flash both USB nodes once before the same15s settling. Different initialization/warm-up and time-varying radio inputs remain confounds in an inter-phase comparison.
Raw measurement distributions are shown alongside reports. B-stream raw versus filtered C++ replay holds its captured inputs fixed, separating local math from between-phase input changes.

Replay uses accepted measurement emissions and own-report emission times reconstructed from USB queue delay, preserving serial FIFO across millisecond timestamp backsteps. Startup cache is unknown; the first15s are excluded.

Network availability comes from the actual demo/accuracy.ts Monitor model separately for each observer, including six cache entries and their exact freshness expiries. Local own-report availability is a separate metric.
Origin report age includes input age, so fresh report bytes can contain older measurements. Filtered reports truthfully carry the oldest selected age.
Node ranging failure fractions cover first-to-last diagnostic snapshots; adding nodes double-counts exchanges. Missing quality records and RX/decode counts do not establish network packet loss.

Reported settings/boot checks cover direct USB identities; N3 boot continuity is inferred from origin reports. Physical placement and environmental stability are operator-confirmed, not independently observed.
Lower stationary scatter does not establish accuracy. The filter retains its demonstrated motion delay and raw-geometry fallback behavior; no threshold is tuned to this hardware ABA.
